# Always Keep a Project Memory

_Applies when: working in any project on either target — the memory half of the close ritual._

Every project has a persistent memory, and it is **always written to** — not only when something
feels noteworthy. A session must never end leaving the project memory empty or stale. This is the
durable thread that survives across sessions and short-lived subagents whose context is discarded.

## The rule

- **Maintain a per-project memory store.** Create it on first work if missing, then append: a
  `memory/` folder at the project root with a `MEMORY.md` index plus one markdown file per fact
  (the agent-core memory convention).
- **Write an entry for every task of substance** — decisions and their "why", constraints and
  context discovered, gotchas hit, what changed and why. Default to writing, not skipping.
- Keep entries **durable and non-obvious**: capture what is not recoverable from the code, the diff,
  or git history. Convert relative dates to absolute. Link related entries.
- Before adding, check the index for an entry to **update** instead — refine, don't duplicate;
  delete entries that turn out wrong.

Target note: on OpenCode the orchestrator-only model makes this the *only* durable thread — see
`61-memory-discipline-opencode` for the session-start scaffold specific to that target.
